title: Sub-MHz SWAP spectroscopy of two-level systems in superconducting qubits
authors: Joaquin Minguzzi, John Clai Owens, Oskar Painter, Matthew H. Matheny, Loren J. Swenson
abstract: An outstanding challenge in superconducting quantum circuits is mitigating loss from two-level system (TLS) defects. SWAP spectroscopy with flux-tunable qubits can detect individual TLSs, but the Rabi chevrons that signal coherent exchange have been observed only for the most strongly coupled defects. Here, we introduce a sequence with fast flux pulses only at state preparation and readout, switched off during the energy-relaxation delay for finer frequency resolution and longer interaction times. We detect Rabi chevrons at swap rates as low as 0.1 MHz, an order of magnitude lower than previously reported. In the dressed-state picture, we fit the coherent swap oscillations to extract the TLS energy-relaxation time. These Rabi chevrons reveal coherent TLSs with a median energy-relaxation time of 10 microseconds, at coupling strengths previously associated with incoherent TLSs. The swap coherence times exceed the qubit T2* limited by flux noise, indicating that the dressed gap protects them from low-frequency 1/f noise.
summary: This paper reports on an advanced SWAP spectroscopy technique to study TLS defects in superconducting qubits. By using fast flux pulses, the researchers achieved unprecedented sensitivity, detecting coherent TLS dynamics at very low coupling strengths. This work significantly advances the understanding of decoherence mechanisms, which is crucial for building reliable quantum computers.
main_problem: The primary challenge is mitigating energy loss from Two-Level System (TLS) defects in superconducting qubits while achieving high-resolution spectroscopy of these defects.
main_result: The authors successfully detected coherent TLS dynamics at swap rates as low as 0.1 MHz, revealing TLSs with a median energy-relaxation time of 10 microseconds.
method: They introduced a fast flux pulse sequence for SWAP spectroscopy, allowing for fine frequency resolution and long interaction times to probe weak coupling regimes.
model_or_system: The system involves flux-tunable superconducting qubits coupled to TLS defects. The dynamics are analyzed using a dressed-state picture, fitting the coherent swap oscillations to extract relaxation times.
key_observables: Rabi chevrons, swap rates (0.1 MHz), TLS energy-relaxation time ($T_{relax}$), and swap coherence time ($T_{osc}$).
important_parameters: Sub-MHz frequency resolution, detection of coherence at rates an order of magnitude lower than previously reported.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting the time-domain population decay ($P_1(	au)$) to a three-component model involving oscillation, relaxation, and background decay.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SWAP spectroscopy technique, comparing previous detection limits ($\gtrsim 5$ MHz) to the new capability ($\downarrow 0.1$ MHz), and show the fitted time traces revealing oscillations and exponential decay.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the problem of TLS loss to detailing the novel fast-flux pulse sequence, presenting the measurements of low-rate Rabi chevrons, and finally analyzing the extracted coherence and relaxation times.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly sensitive experimental platform for characterizing decoherence sources in superconducting qubits, directly impacting the feasibility and fidelity of quantum computation.
